article.title: Your National Political Committee newsletter — Cool Fall Organizing
article.author: DSA National: NPC Dispatch and Newsletter
article.content: Enjoy your September National Political Committee (NPC) newsletter! Our NPC is an elected 27-person body (including both YDSA Co-Chairs) which functions as the board of directors of DSA. This month, hear about hot labor updates, organizing trainings, volunteer opportunities, and more! And to make sure you get our newsletters in your inbox, sign up here! Each one features action alerts, upcoming events, political education, and more. From the National Political Committee — Cool Fall Organizing Sunday 9/27 — How Should DSA Respond to Data Centers? RSVP for our DSA Labor Call! Work for DSA! Application Deadlines Begin Friday 9/18 Sign Up for Fall 2026 Emergency Tenant Organizing Committee Training Series! Classes Begin Saturday 10/24 Mutual Aid Working Group Reforms Disaster Relief Committee — Get Involved Sign Up for National Political Education Commission Newsletter Housing Justice Commission Abolish Rent Book Club — Final Sessions Still Open Contribute to Democratic Left! From the National Political Committee — Cool Fall Organizing It’s September again, and while hot socialist summer is over, there’s lots of cool organizing going into the fall. From chapter Labor Day celebrations, to back-to-school organizing, to worker solidarity actions you can do right now, DSA members like you are getting in gear across the country! We spent Labor Day weekend with hundreds of DSA members in Chicago at the annual Socialism Conference organized by Haymarket Books, which is a great opportunity for political education and big-picture strategizing across organizations on the left. DSA members were represented on over 20 panels, including ones on organizing a general strike and building a stronger pro-democracy labor movement, and showcasing our own “Workers Deserve More” program with special guest Hasan Piker. In DSA, we always want to focus on outward-facing work that builds our power with more and more people, but it’s important to make time to keep learning and testing each others’ ideas too! This spring, over 170 DSA chapters participated in May Day actions. And last week, chapters came out to organize and celebrate workers — check out some of our highlights here! From NEPA DSA’s Labor Rally in Scranton, Pennsylvania, to Greater Baltimore’s Labor Day Potluck, to Northern Colorado’s Labor Night Out, DSA members came together to create community and showcase worker wins. And check out some photo and video highlights! Boston DSA showed that socialism beats fascism Middle Tennessee DSA Labor Day marchers said Workers Deserve More Miami DSA’s Labor Day highlight was their most ambitious Leftist Movie Night of the year: a special 90th anniversary screening of Charlie Chaplin’s Modern Times Socialist socializing like these Labor Day events create organizing opportunities! DSA members understand that bringing people together helps start conversations about how we can organize our workplace, protect our communities, elect socialist candidates, and more. (That’s probably why the Wall Street Journal set out to make coffee with comrades scary!) And our Young Democratic Socialists of America (YDSA) Fall Drive is off to a great start. Since last semester, more than 45 new campuses have started YDSA chapters. And since the beginning of August, YDSA has doubled its membership! Last year, YDSA chapters organized to protect immigrant students, support campus worker unions, end student lunch debt, and more. From the University of Florida YDSA’s kicking the Department of Homeland Security out of their Career Fair, to YDSA at the University of Delaware successfully pressuring the administration to stop collaborating with ICE, to University of Oregon YDSA winning medication access on campus, YDSA students are making big wins and learning how to organize long-lasting campaigns. That’s why they’re growing so much! And given the rise of right-wing campus outreach, we need our youth organizers more than ever. And speaking of fall labor solidarity… we’re boycotting Starbucks this pumpkin spice season! Take the boycott pledge with our DSA National Labor Commission and DSA members across the country. In solidarity with over 12,000 baristas across the country with Starbucks Workers United, DSA has pledged to operate as a Starbucks-free political organization during the duration of the boycott. This means that Starbucks products shall not be purchased with DSA funds for meetings, conferences, trainings, offices, conventions, or other official events. You can hear from Starbucks workers about the boycott here. Solidarity work like this is one reason that thousands of people are joining DSA and renewing their memberships. They see members like you showing up and doing the work our communities need! Would you like to reach out to other members about renewing their dues? Sign up for one of our Fall Drive phonebanks! Training is provided on the call. Sunday 9/27 at 5pm ET/4pm CT/3pm MT/2pm PT with special guest Professor Richard Wolff. One lucky phonebanker will receive a signed copy of Professor Wolff’s book Understanding Socialism! Wednesday 10/7 at 7pm ET/6pm CT/5pm MT/4pm PT with special guest David Griscom. One lucky phonebanker will receive a signed copy of David Griscom’s book The Myth of Red Texas! And read on for more ways to stand up for a brighter, more democratic future! Solidarity, Ashik Siddique and Megan Romer DSA National Co-Chairs PS: last week, more than 1000 people joined us for “End Times Fascism:” A DSA Conversation with Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor. Check out the book talk video here! Sunday 9/27 — How Should DSA Respond to Data Centers? RSVP for our DSA Labor Call! The construction of data centers around the country is leading to ecological damage and skyrocketing electricity costs, causing grassroots coalitions to take a stand and in some states, win moratoriums on new construction. But for unionized workers in the trades, data centers have led to new contracts and renewed investments in apprenticeships. Join DSA’s National Labor Commission Sunday 9/27 at 1pm ET/12pm CT/11am MT/10am PT for Building the Machine: The Trades and Anti-Data Center Organizing! On the call, you’ll hear the perspectives of anti-data center organizers and rank-and-file union workers about how socialist unionists should orient to the data center boom. Work for DSA! Application Deadlines Begin Friday 9/18 DSA is hiring! Please apply if you’re interested, or send to someone you know who has the right experience. Open positions include: Regional Organizer (rolling; first deadline 9/18) Membership Growth and Retention Coordinator (deadline 9/20) Designer (deadline 9/25) You can learn more about these positions on our Careers page here. Sign Up for Fall 2026 Emergency Tenant Organizing Committee Training Series! Classes Begin Saturday 10/24 The Housing Justice Commission is proud to announce that our 2026 Fall Emergency Tenant Organizing Committee (ETOC) cohort is now accepting RSVPs from prospective tenant organizers. ETOC is a DSA initiative to promote the formation of militant tenant unions through tenant-to-tenant training and instruction. This ETOC cohort will teach you the fundamentals of tenant organizing over a series of 4 meetings in October and November. The series starts Saturday 10/24 at 2pm ET/1pm CT/12pm MT/11am PT. RSVP today! Instruction will focus on giving you the skills you need to develop new tenant unions that will organize tenants on a citywide or regional scale. We encourage you to invite others you intend to organize a tenant union with. Mutual Aid Working Group Reforms Disaster Relief Committee — Get Involved The Mutual Aid Working Group (MAWG) is reforming the Disaster Relief Committee! MAWG’s Disaster Relief Committee will organize MAWG members to collaborate on disaster preparedness, awareness, and relief. If you would like to get involved in this new committee, or other work in MAWG, join the working group! Sign Up for National Political Education Commission Newsletter Don’t get left behind on the left! Keep up with DSA’s National Political Education Commission — with popular trainings, debates and events, national reading groups, media, commentary, and more — by signing up for our monthly missive, Red Letter! Housing Justice Commission Abolish Rent Book Club — Final Sessions Still Open Join DSA members and tenant organizers around the country for a nationwide reading of the book Abolish Rent, written by two co-founders of the Los Angeles Tenants Union, Tracy Rosenthal and Leonardo Vilchis. Sessions have already started, but there’s still spots for the Wednesday 9/30 and Wednesday 10/14 meetings. Book club meetings will be at 8pm ET/7pm CT/6pm MT/5pm PT. Together, we’ll learn from the book, share our experiences as tenants and organizers, and discuss how to create a world where rent doesn’t exist. Use the discount code in the signup link here link for a discount on a copy of the book! Contribute to Democratic Left! Democratic Left, DSA’s official news publication, is opening applications for non-editorial board roles. If you are interested in supporting Democratic Left’s movement journalism as a book reviewer, reporter, arts critic, copy editor, graphic designer, or chapter correspondent, please fill out the third form linked on this page on the DSA forum.
